rich_summary: Arjuna resists a proposal he sees as sinful and urges that Draupadi be properly married according to virtue and seniority. Yet after the brothers gaze upon Draupadi, her extraordinary beauty stirs desire in all of them. Yudhishthira perceives the tension and, recalling Vyasa’s words and fearing division among the brothers, declares that Draupadi will be the common wife of all five Pandavas. Soon after, Krishna and Balarama secretly visit the disguised brothers in the potter’s house, recognizing their true identity despite their concealment and offering quiet encouragement. Meanwhile Dhrishtadyumna secretly observes their humble domestic life, where Kunti instructs Draupadi in household duties. His report to King Drupada begins to reveal that the mysterious Brahmins who won Draupadi are in fact the Pandavas, setting the stage for a politically and morally unusual marriage.

highlight_spans.why: Arjuna rejects participation in an act he believes sinful, framing the moral tension around Draupadi's marriage.
The moment when Draupadi’s beauty overwhelms the brothers and awakens desire, driving the coming decision.
Yudhishthira’s decisive declaration that Draupadi will be the common wife of all five Pandavas.
Krishna recognizes the Pandavas despite their disguise, reinforcing his role as a perceptive ally and guide.
The humble domestic scene where Kunti instructs Draupadi in distributing food reveals the Pandavas’ disguised life and emerging family order.

top_scenes.scene_text: Yudhishthira solemnly declares that Draupadi will be the common wife of the five brothers while the Pandavas stand around the radiant princess in a dim hut.
Krishna and Balarama entering the potter’s hut and greeting the disguised Pandavas, recognizing them despite their simple clothing.
Night in the potter’s house: the Pandavas lying on kusa grass beds while Draupadi rests near their feet and Dhrishtadyumna secretly watches from the shadows.
